old_title: Transfer news LIVE: Guimaraes nears Arsenal move, Vinicius Jr latest
new_title: Transfer news LIVE: Arsenal identify Vinicius Jr alternatives
old_text:
Bruno Guimaraes has received permission to travel to Arsenal and complete his £75m move from Newcastle United. The 28-year-old midfielder will undergo a medical at the Premier League champions within the coming days after both clubs agreed a fee with an announcement of his signing expected shortly afterwards.
The deal represents a key piece of business of Mikel Arteta ahead of Arsenal's title defence - while Newcastle will be left to wave goodbye to another key player following the departures of Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali this summer.
Arsenal will now turn to continuing their pursuit of Guimaraes' international team-mate Vinicius Jr, although the Gunners believe it is increasingly likely that he stays at Real Madrid, who have significantly upped their new contract offer to the Brazilian star.
Liverpool, meanwhile, want to sign Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and have also lined up his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye in what could be a double swoop for Andoni Iraola's side. The European champions may be willing to let them go with Maghnes Akliouche is set to join from Monaco.
Elsewhere, Manchester United want to sign a left-back with Lewis Hall reportedly now set on a move to Old Trafford, but Newcastle are determined to stop the exodus and insist he is not for sale.
Follow all of the latest news, rumours and done deals with our live blog below:
Arsenal close in on Guimaraes with £75m fee agreed
Arsenal's move for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes is finally nearing completion.
The Gunners are confident of finally singing the 28-year-old midfielder, whose future has been the subject of frenzied speculation for weeks ever since it emerged that he had indicated that he wanted to leave Tyneside for the Emirates Stadium.
Guimaraes reported for duty at Newcastle's pre-season training camp in La Manga in Spain on Monday, just hours after Newcastle rejected an opening bid from Arsenal.
It now appears that significant progress has been made with the Premier League champions closing in on a cut-price £75m deal which would see them finally capture a man they have long coveted.
Good morning!
Welcome to The Independent's coverage of today's latest transfer news and gossip.
Newcastle officially have a new manager who will be keen to stop the exodus of players this summer while Arsenal continue to make shrewd signings as they aim to defend their Premier League title.
Liverpool are in the market for two PSG players and Man Utd are attempting to bring in defensive cover at left-back.
Let's get stuck into it...
The real reason Chelsea signed Jordan Henderson
Jordan Henderson's move to Chelsea represents one of the more peculiar transfers of the summer. But dig a little deeper and the logic becomes at least more convincing. A player in the twilight of a glittering career is returning to one of the biggest clubs in Europe. Awkward spells with Al-Ettifaq and Ajax were followed by a more productive and defined role in an excellent Brentford season last term.
Man United Women appoint Eva Olid as new head coach after Marc Skinner exit
Manchester United Women have announced the appointment of Eva Olid as their new head coach on an initial two-year deal with the option of a further year.
Vinicius Jr reveals what Jose Mourinho told him as he weighs up his future amid Arsenal links
Vinicius Jr has revealed that new Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho encouraged him to maintain his "happy" and "joyful" approach to football as the Brazil international navigates ongoing speculation about his future at the Bernabéu.
Why is Mohamed Salah signing for Trabzonspor?
The Liverpool icon, who left Anfield as a free agent at the end of last season, has arrived in Turkey ahead of the move and has been pictured by the club wearing the team's colours ahead of signing his contract on Thursday. He will wear the number 61 shirt at his new club.
Real Madrid legend implores 'deceitful' Gianni Infantino to resign as Fifa president
Luis Figo has implored Gianni Infantino to resign as pressure mounts on the much-criticised Fifa president following his foiled attempts to sell stakes in the World Cup.
Infantino was forced to abandon his plans - namely to sell stakes in the World Cup and other Fifa tournaments to private investors - after public uproar last week, with Uefa confirming a boycott of Fifa events if the plan was voted through.
Man United set to offload two goalkeepers as Michael Carrick's squad overhaul gathers pace
Manchester United are poised to offload two goalkeepers, with Radek Vitek set to join Middlesbrough in a deal potentially worth up to £14 million, while Altay Bayindir prepares for a loan move to Celta Vigo.
Vitek, a 22-year-old Czech shot-stopper, is nearing a permanent switch to last season's Championship play-off finalists Middlesbrough following an impressive loan spell at Bristol City.
Kang-In reacts to Atletico move
South Korea winger Lee Kang-In spoke about joining Atletico Madrid
The 25-year-old signed a five-year contract with the LaLiga side who paid around €40m to PSG.
He said "I'm very pleased and very happy to join this great club, with a lot of desire for everything, to meet my team-mates, to know the club, to know the coach, to meet the entire coaching staff and then to meet fans who have told me that they are the best in the world."
Juventus pursuing Zirkzee
Juventus are said to be interested in Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee and hope to bring the forward in on a loan deal.
Zirkzee is down the pecking order under Michael Carrick and could be keen on the move though the right deal will need to be struck for all parties.
Juve have already signed Randal Kolo Muani and Kerim Alajbegovic so there is no urgency on their part to get Zirkee's move done.
new_text:
Rodri looks set to leave Manchester City amid interest from Barcelona and Real Madrid. The World Cup winning captain is into the final year of his contract and favours a move to Barca who are in negotiations over a €45m fee.
Arsenal were dealt a blow in one of their summer transfer pursuits as Vinicius Jr has signed a contract extension with Real Madrid. The Gunners have moved on from targeting the winger and have reignited their interest in Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez while PSG's Bradley Barcola is also on their list.
In more positive news, Bruno Guimaraes has completed a medical at Arsenal ahead of his £75m move from Newcastle United. The 28-year-old midfielder is now expected to be announced as a new Gooner on Friday ahead of Arsenal's pre-season fixtures this weekend. The deal represents a key piece of business of Mikel Arteta ahead of Arsenal's title defence.
Liverpool, meanwhile, also want to sign Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and have also lined up his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye in what could be a double swoop for Andoni Iraola's side. The European champions may be willing to let them go especially following Maghnes Akliouche signing from Monaco.
Elsewhere, Manchester United have added to their ranks by bringing in a teenage midfielder and they are exploring their options at left-back with Lewis Hall reportedly now set on a move to Old Trafford, but Newcastle are determined to stop the exodus and insist he is not for sale.
Follow all of the latest news, rumours and done deals with our live blog below:
Rodri set to leave Manchester City?
He claims that the two clubs are in negotiations over a fee with Barca willing to pay more than €45m and Man City perhaps wanting a higher price.
Rodri wants the move and will choose Barcelona over Real Madrid who also hold an interest in Spain's World Cup winning captain.
Announcement expected for Bruno Guimaraes
Bruno Guimaraes will become an Arsenal player.
The Gunners agreed a £75m fee for the influential midfielder who underwent a medical on Thursday ahead of his expected move from Newcastle.
It's a big signing for Mikel Arteta's men and an announcement confirming the transfer is expected before the weekend and probably likely to happen at some point today.
Would Williams work for Arsenal?
We're back with The Sun who don't have any details but are instead speculating whether Arsenal could turn their attention to Nico Williams.
The Gunners have shown interest in the Spanish winger before and he is thought to have a release clause of around £77m in his contract.
That seems more in line with Arsenal's spending habits which makes him a realistic alternative after the Gunners missed out on Vinicius Jr.
Barcola on Arsenal's radar
More alternatives are creeping out for Arsenal now that their pursuit of Vinicius Jr is over.
The Sun believe that Maghnes Akliouche's arrival at PSG, on a €50m move, means the French champions will be more willing to sell players.
That could have a knock on effect for the future of Bradley Barcola.
Liverpool are said to be in pole position to sign the winger but Arsenal have previously been interested in his services though they remain a way off in terms of valuations.
PSG rate him at around £130m and Arsenal are nowhere as high in their own valuations.
Arsenal identify Vinicius Jr alternatives
Vinicius Jr's contract extension with Real Madrid was a blow to Arsenal as there had been serious interest and confidence that a deal could be done.
Alas, that was not to be the case and the Gunners have swiftly moved their attentions elsewhere with The Standard reporting that they have already agreed personal terms with Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez.
They cite a report from Bem Jacobs that Alvarez has been seen as Arsenal's back up in case the Vinicius Jr move didn't pay off as well as other rumours from X (formerly Twitter), over the personal terms being agreed.
I'd take that last part with a pinch of slat but Arsenal's interest in Alvarez has been long-standing.
The Atletico striker is said to favour a switch to Barcelona but has not ruled out a return to the Premier League.
Good morning!
Welcome to The Independent's coverage of today's latest transfer news and gossip.
Arsenal's pursuit of Vinicius Jr is over after the winger signed a new deal with Real Madrid on Thursday. That means the Gunners are looking of alternative options and have reportedly landed back on Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez.
They also hold an interest in Bradley Barcola though Liverpool are closer to securing a deal for the PSG forward.
Man Utd, meanwhile, have signed a surprising midfielder and are in the market for left-back cover.
We'll go through all the latest rumours and done deals throughout the day so let's begin...
Uefa doubles down on Fifa boycott but holds greater weapon to unseat Gianni Infantino
Uefa and other key stakeholders in European football are intent on doubling down on their plan to unseat Gianni Infantino as Fifa president, with boycotts and non co-operation set to continue, to the point of potentially making the global game "ungovernable".
The Swiss official is himself determined to stay in his position, as illustrated by Wednesday's defiant Fifa statement. Infantino is aware he still has the numbers to win March's election.
Uefa nevertheless signalled its own intent by stating that Fifa's response so far does not meet the threshold for their boycott of Fifa competitions to be lifted, specifically pointing to how there have not been "assurances" that attempts like the privatisation of the World Cup "to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again".
Atletico confident they can beat Inter to Romero signature
Atletico Madrid are confident they can beat Inter Milan to the signing of Cristian Romero, according to The Times.
Inter have a broad agreement with Tottenham over a deal for the departing defender, but Atletico feel the Argentine would rather join them.
Vinicius Jr signs Real Madrid contract extension to end Arsenal hopes
Vinicius Jr has penned a contract extension with Real Madrid until 2032, ending Arsenal's hopes of signing the Brazilian superstar this summer.
Premier League champions Arsenal were hopeful of acquiring Vinicius in a statement move, looking to poach the winger who had one year left on his contract at the Santiago Bernabeu.
Their interest came as contract negotiations between Vinicius and Madrid were stalling, with there initially being considerable distance in stances on a new deal as Vinicius' camp demanded a proposal comparable to Kylian Mbappe's.
But as Arsenal made progress in negotiations, Real Madrid upped their offer to convince Vinicius to sign on the dotted line and stay put, which was the preference for both the Spanish giants and the player.
Real Madrid to put two Man Utd targets up for sale?
Real Madrid could make two Manchester United targets available for purchase - French midfielders Aurelien Tchouameni and Eduardo Camavinga - in order to free up funds so they can sign Spain midfielder Rodri from Manchester City, according to El Nacional.
This comes after reports that Barcelona are growing in confidence that they can successfully pip their rivals to the signing of Rodri, who are set to make an approach.
